Dreieck.et: From drei + Ecke. Displaced non-native Triangel, from Latin triangulum.

dreizehn.et: From Middle High German dreizehen, from Old High German drīzehan, akin to Old Saxon thriutein. Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *þritehun. Equivalent to drei + zehn. Compare Dutch dertien, West Frisian trettjin, English thirteen, Danish tretten.

s: Er ist noch unter dreißig Jahre alt.
He is still under thirty years old.
dreißig.et: From Middle High German drīzic, from Old High German drīzzug, from Proto-Germanic *þrīz tigiwiz. Equivalent to drei + -zig.

Dreitagebart.et: From drei + Tage + Bart, literally “three-days beard”.

Dreikönigsfest.et: From drei + König + -s- + Fest. Literally, “three kings' festival”.

s: bold, brash, audacious, impudent (without respect or restraint)
dreist.et: Borrowed from Middle Low German drîste, from Old Saxon thrīsti, from Proto-West Germanic *þrīstī.

s: love triangle, ménage à trois (a love relationship involving three persons)

dreißigste.et: From Middle High German drīzigeste, drīzegeste, from Old High German drīzugōsto, equivalent to dreißig + -ste.

Dreikäsehoch.et: Univerbation of drei + Käse + hoch, literally “three cheeses high/tall”. Compare French haut comme trois pommes and Czech trpaslík.

Dreifaltigkeit.et: From Middle High German drīvaltecheit f, from drīvaltec (“triune”) + -heit, from drīvalt (“threefold”) + -eg, from Old High German thrī̌falt, from thrī (“three”) + -falt. Equivalent to dreifaltig + -keit.
